questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Vienna seemed both perfectly close to and perfectly far away from Copenhagen both in terms of distance and culture. Additionally, it is very easy to travel to neighboring countries from Vienna which I planned to from the start. I also thought learning some German would be fun.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. The university gave the necessary information about semester start in advance and in simple terms. Anything I was unsure about I could find out on the university's website. Access to information about registration of residence with the authorities was also sufficient.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had sent a mail about choosing an orientation session. At the orientation session the important things were discussed and you could ask any questions you might have had.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't difficult to find housing. At least not when starting the search some months in advance. I signed up for dorms and got a few offers. I ended up going with an apartment I found through Housing Anywhere, though. How attractive the rent and location of each tenancy is varies a lot. I would recommend starting the search in good time and look for a somewhat central place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is only off campus. Public transportation is great and cheap (buy a semester ticket for 75 euro) so keep that in mind when choosing a place. Also, booking a place through Housing Anywhere will cost a fee, and the landlord might require another fee on top of that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many different types of places available. That being said, the most attractive ones were probably gone after a short while. My impression was that the housing situation was similar to that of (international students in) Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was simple. The only thing that took a bit of time (30 minutes) was finding a validating machine for my u:card (student ID) but we found it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: If I remember correctly, the registration process was simply attending your orientation session and validating the u:card they give you there. Registering for courses was done through u:space. Here, it's notable that you could sign up for as many courses as you wanted. It was a simple process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university was always available to answer questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything I wanted, although these courses differed a bit from my originally intended choices because of scheduling conflicts.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sign up for more courses than you need. I signed up for twice as many. It's a bit of a puzzle to figure out which courses conflict with each other and to what degree. This is important to look at before making your final choices as many courses require regular attendance to pass. Also keep in mind that you may have a lot of exams during the last week depending on your courses. I made sure to spread mine out so I essentially had half my "exams" before Christmas break. The form of examination varies a lot, too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were different from what I had met before which was nice. They were also not that demanding which left time for leisure activities.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Like I said, the level of the courses was generally lower than for (mandatory courses) at the University of Copenhagen. It felt a little superficial sometimes, but that might be because the courses are smaller (2-4 ECTS). However, among the courses I had, a few were probably closer to what I'm used to in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more lecture based. The teachers were open to questions, and in some courses the grade depends on participation, but it was still less interactive than I was used to. In a few of my courses, the lessons would start with going through the homework which I found to be unusual. Some courses will have you do a presentation with a partner, but the law campus doesn't have good study spaces for that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Drafting and Negotiating Cross-border M&A and Joint Venture Contracts because the teacher was very competent and made the subject interesting. I would also recommend Anglo-American Legal English I and V simply because I found it very interesting to learn about American, UK and Austrian/German law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Sausages were perhaps a bit more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You can sign up for Uni sports. They have a lot of different things at different levels. Keep in mind that this is not exclusive to international students. I was the only non-German speaker but people are nice and can speak English as well.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are quite a few events arranged by the Erasmus Student Network ("ESN", not the university).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going on a wine hike with ESN. It's a great experience and you can meet all kinds of people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going on trips through ESN. I went on a trip of theirs to Slovenia one weekend which was amazing. Generally, I think Vienna is perfect for travelling to different places. I also went to Budapest and Bratislava which was awesome.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. Austrians aren't so different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for Uni Sports, talk to Austrians in class or meet them at bars, I guess.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I felt like Austrians often (not always) waited until the doors had opened before even beginning to exit the tram/subway/bus. This was annoying when the subway was crowded, for example.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I found them to be friendly and proper. I liked the food as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find a (somewhat) central place to live. Avoid choosing courses with overlapping exams. And travel.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Often, the courses will not require that you buy a book, but some might. To avoid spending a needless amount of money on books you might want to try to find and borrow them at the local library instead. I saved money by buying a library card (10 euro) instead of two books.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from a lot of different countries, visiting new countries and trying great food.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I lived with two roommates, one of which I didn't like. It was a challenge to confront and live with someone like him. It was also unexpected to me that written exams meant having to write in hand, and information about how long an exam was or whether it was open book was not always given until the exam itself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Vienna is a beautiful city, and I'm glad I chose to go there. It's warm in the summer and cold in the winter, but I had a great time the whole stay.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
